note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a ROK 4, 5, 10; A06b ROK 4, 5, 10; L05 ROK 15): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, South Korea, 2024
sources.said: Person has been domiciled in South Korea for a continuous period of 5 years and has permanent residence status. ... Renunciation of citizenship of a foreign country (unless unreasonable to request). ... Person has voluntarily acquired citizenship of another country. Does not apply in the following cases if the person makes a declaration within 6 months of acquiring foreign citizenship to retain South Korean citizenship: person acquired the same citizenship as the spouse through marriage, the citizenship of an adoptive parent, the citizenship of another country after acknowledgment by a foreign father or mother, or the person is a minor child or spouse of a citizen who lost citizenship due to the acquisition of citizenship of another country.
